data.long_meaning: Rangnath is a Sanskrit name which means 'Lord of Colors'. It is a revered name for Lord Vishnu and Lord Rama, symbolizing their omnipresence and all-encompassing nature. The name Rangnath carries the meaning “Lord of Colors” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Rangnath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of colors and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rangnath represents the divine presence of Lord Vishnu and Lord Rama in all aspects of life, inspiring devotion, faith, and a deep sense of spiritual connection.
data.etymology: Rangnath belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Colors.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rangnath total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rangnath holds significant cultural relevance in Hinduism, particularly in the region of South India and Nepal where Lord Vishnu, known as Ranganatha, is widely worshipped. According to legend, Lord Vishnu takes the form of Ranganatha, lying on the serpent Ananta, in the Ranganathaswamy Temple at Srirangam. Devotees believe that Lord Ranganatha's name encapsulates His universal nature and His ability to bring color and joy to every aspect of life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rangnath resonates with the spiritual belief that the divine is not limited to any one form or color but transcends all. When referred to Lord Vishnu, it represents His playful and brilliant nature, as the dispeller of darkness and the embodiment of love, compassion, and wisdom. Similarly, when applied to Lord Rama, it symbolizes His virtuous qualities of truthfulness, loyalty, and strength. Ultimately, the name Rangnath serves as a constant reminder of the omnipresence and omnipotence of the divine and inspires devotees to embrace the richness of life and the world around them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rangnath: Lord of Colors. Symbolizes the divine play of colors in creation and the inner radiance of the soul.
